title: The Net Mender
text: An old woman mends nets on a stilt-house over the marsh, her fingers quick, humming to herself. The nets hang drying all around, and they are full. Not of fish. Of shoes, hands, a doll, a crown. Her nets catch whatever the water takes.

options.label: The one with the sea in them helps her haul, and the water gives up what it holds.

outcomes.text: The net comes up heavy with a drowned knight's gear, and nothing of the knight. She does not seem surprised.

options.label: The one with the hurt arm lets her bind it in net-cord, and does not ask what she hums.

outcomes.text: Old marsh-craft. It holds, and it costs, and the humming stays in their head.

options.label: Cut her nets loose, and free whatever the water took.

outcomes.text: Whatever was in them swims free, and it remembers you.
